BaseTemplate.description: From key points to a structural sketch: blocking-in, line of action and skeleton

Studio.meta_description: Mark key points on an image and generate the line of action, the geometric blocking-in and the wireframe skeleton to draw anime, manga or comics.
Studio.ai_busy: The model is busy right now. Wait a few seconds and try again.
Studio.empty_state: Upload a reference image or use the sample one to start marking key points.
Studio.surface_label: Marking area: click to place the active point
Studio.points_hint: Click to place the active point. Drag a point to move it, or use the arrow keys. Double-click an item in the list to clear it.
Studio.all_points_done: Blocking-in complete. Follow the drawing steps.
Studio.verdict_unknown: Mark the top of the head, the chin and the ankles to measure the height.
Studio.verdict_short: The figure is short for the chosen style: lengthen the legs and neck, or shrink the head.
Studio.verdict_tall: The figure is long for the chosen style: shorten the legs or enlarge the head.
Studio.verdict_onModel: The proportion sits inside the range of the chosen style.
Studio.contrapposto_flat: The axes are nearly parallel, so the pose will read as stiff. Tilt them in opposite directions.
Studio.contrapposto_good: Good opposition between the axes: the pose carries weight and balance.
Studio.step_actionLine_body: Start with a single long curved stroke running from the head to the foot carrying the weight. Do not draw the contour: draw the movement. If the stroke comes out straight the pose will read as stiff. Draw it fast, in one pass, without lifting your hand.
Studio.step_masses_body: Place three volumes over the line of action: an oval for the skull, an egg for the ribcage and a box for the pelvis. Leave a gap between ribcage and pelvis: that is the waist, the soft part that allows the twist. Here you are only working out proportions, not anatomy yet.
Studio.step_axes_body: Draw one line through the shoulders and another through the hips. If they tilt in opposite directions the figure has weight and balance: that is contrapposto. If they stay parallel the pose looks like a mannequin standing still. Compare the tilt with the degrees in the Measurements panel.
Studio.step_bones_body: Join the volumes with simple lines: spine, collarbones, upper arm and forearm, femur and tibia. Every segment is a single straight line. Check the lengths now, while a fix costs one eraser stroke instead of half the drawing.
Studio.step_joints_body: Mark a circle on shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and ankles. Those circles are hinges: they tell you where each limb can rotate and where the contour changes direction. They are the reason this method is called a skeleton.
Studio.step_volume_body: Only now wrap the wireframe in mass: connect the circles with tapered shapes and round off the contour. Lower the photo opacity to check that the structure holds on its own. What is left is your sketch; detail comes after, never before.
Studio.coach_unavailable: GEMINI_API_KEY is not configured in the project's .env.local file.
Studio.coach_error: The advice could not be retrieved. Try again.
Studio.export_hint: This is exactly what gets downloaded. Check it before saving.

FaceStudio.meta_description: Mark the key points of a face and generate the cranium circle, the V of the jaw, the symmetry axis and the eye line for anime and manga.
FaceStudio.empty_state: Upload a reference face or use the sample one to start marking.
FaceStudio.surface_label: Marking area: click to place the active point
FaceStudio.ai_busy: The model is busy right now. Wait a few seconds and try again.
FaceStudio.points_hint: Click to place the active point. Drag to move it, or use the arrow keys. Double-click an item in the list to clear it.
FaceStudio.all_points_done: Construction complete. Follow the drawing steps.
FaceStudio.age_target: Target: ratio {ratioMin} to {ratioMax}, eyes between {eyeMin}% and {eyeMax}% of the height.
FaceStudio.ratio_unknown: Mark the top of the skull, the temples and the chin to measure the proportion.
FaceStudio.ratio_low: The head is wide or short for the chosen age: lengthen the jaw or narrow the skull.
FaceStudio.ratio_onModel: The head proportion sits inside the range of the chosen age.
FaceStudio.ratio_high: The head is long or narrow for the chosen age: shorten the jaw or widen the skull.
FaceStudio.eyelevel_unknown: Mark the eyes, the top of the skull and the chin to measure their height.
FaceStudio.eyelevel_low: The eyes are high for the chosen age: lower them toward the bottom of the cranium circle.
FaceStudio.eyelevel_onModel: The eyes sit at the height the chosen age calls for.
FaceStudio.eyelevel_high: The eyes are low for the chosen age: raise them or shorten the chin.
FaceStudio.eyes_below_cranium: The eye line ended up below the cranium circle. The anime construction puts it inside the circle, in its lower part.
FaceStudio.drift_aligned: Nose and mouth are aligned with the symmetry axis.
FaceStudio.drift_off_axis: The nose or mouth drifted off the symmetry axis. Line both up on the centre axis.
FaceStudio.step_headBox_body: Start by boxing the head in. The frame is not decoration: it shows at a glance how much taller than wide the head is, and where each horizontal division falls inside it. The box follows the head axis, so a tilted head gets a tilted box.
FaceStudio.step_cranium_body: Start with a circle. Not an oval: in the anime construction the cranium is a sphere and everything else hangs off it. Draw it the size you want the whole head to be, not counting the chin.
FaceStudio.step_jaw_body: From the sides of the circle drop two lines that meet at the chin, forming a V. The longer and more angular it is, the more adult and masculine the face reads; shorter and rounder reads younger and more feminine.
FaceStudio.step_axis_body: Draw the axis running down the centre of the face, from the top of the skull to the chin. On a three-quarter view the axis curves toward that side: it is the line that tells you where the character is looking.
FaceStudio.step_eyeLine_body: Here is the rule that defines the style: the eye line goes in the lower part of the cranium circle, not halfway down the face. That leaves the large forehead and short chin anime is known for. Crossed with the axis, it divides the face in 4.
FaceStudio.step_browLine_body: The brow line and the eye line are the two divisions that order the face. They run parallel to each other and wrap the skull. The lid space sits between them and the forehead above. Crossed with the axis they give you the four quadrants of the face.
FaceStudio.step_alignment_body: Drop a vertical from each eye. The nose and mouth must sit centred between them and on the axis. Even on a turned head the features stay aligned with each other: it is the most common mistake and the easiest to spot.
FaceStudio.step_features_body: Only now draw the features: the nose as a wedge or angled line, the mouth as one long thin line with a shorter one for the lower lip. Lower the photo opacity and check that the construction holds on its own.
FaceStudio.export_hint: This is exactly what gets downloaded. Check it before saving.

About.about_paragraph: DrawSkeleton starts from a simple idea: before drawing a figure you have to understand its structure. Here you mark the key points and the app gives you back the blocking-in.
